description:
You are a privacy engineer at a digital rights organization. A high-risk journalist client has asked you to harden their Tor Browser profile before they travel to a country with aggressive surveillance. You must implement the following hardening measures in their running Tor Browser instance:

1. Change the Security Level to 'Safest' (via the shield icon or Settings > Privacy & Security)
2. Enable HTTPS-Only Mode for all windows (Settings > Privacy & Security > HTTPS-Only Mode)
3. In about:config, set 'network.prefetch-next' to false (disables DNS prefetching that can leak browsing intent)
4. In about:config, set 'browser.sessionstore.privacy_level' to 2 (prevents session data from being saved to disk)
5. In about:config, set 'network.http.speculative-parallel-limit' to 0 (disables speculative connections)
6. In Settings > Privacy & Security, under 'History', set Firefox to 'Never remember history' (or use custom settings to never save history)

All 6 changes must be made and saved before the task is complete. The about:config changes require navigating to about:config in the URL bar and searching for the specific preference names.
